refusedRequestsInAppLog.attribution: All 18 are this lane's own negative probes plus the loopback refusal checks (public-auth-probe.json records 7 of them). No scheduler request was ever refused: every AttemptFinished in the raw log beside this artifact carries 200 or 500, never 401 or 403.

concurrencyFinding.what: Two of the ten jobs returned HTTP 500 at 19:40:15Z and 19:40:29Z, AFTER my verification triggers had all passed. Both were AUTHORIZED (the app logged them and refused nothing); they failed on the scraper's own Chromium lock, not on auth.
concurrencyFinding.mechanism: The scraper serializes all browser work behind one `chromium-lock` with a 600s wait timeout. My full-scrape verification run acquired it at 19:28:53Z and held it for 750s. The natural 19:30Z fires of active-wo-report-hourly (19:30:15Z) and wo-manager-sync queued behind it.
evidence: 19:40:13 [active-wo-report] Sync failed: Chromium lock timeout: report-export waited 600s
19:41:05 wo-manager-sync AttemptFinished status=200 (the scheduler's own retry, after the lock freed)
concurrencyFinding.attribution: PROVOKED BY THIS LANE'S OWN VERIFICATION, not by the migration itself: I manually ran the 750s full-scrape in the same half hour as two natural fires. Nothing in the production schedule is guaranteed to overlap this way (full-scrape fires at 05:00/13:00/21:00Z and takes ~13 min when unblocked).
concurrencyFinding.whyItStillMatters: It is a real property of the new topology that the old one did not have. On Cloud Run the lock is per-instance, so concurrent jobs could land on different instances and never contend; on one droplet the lock is global, so any job that runs longer than 600s while another is waiting makes that other job fail with a 500. The retry policy (retryCount 2, 300s min backoff) absorbed the wo-manager-sync case and returned 200 36s later; active-wo-report-hourly spent its retries in the same blocked window.
concurrencyFinding.notAnAuthFailure: Every request involved was authorized. The 500 body came from the sync's own lock timeout.

observations: Every attempt seen in the window for every job carried the correct target: before the repoint the URL was https://smartcity-scraper-494195107606.us-central1.run.app, after it http://159.89.190.154:8080. No attempt after the repoint went to GCP, and no attempt went to a wrong host.

Extra `gcloud scheduler jobs run` calls were made by this machine's GCP identity (empressaioemail@gmail.com) at 19:08:54Z, 19:14:59Z, 19:24:09Z, 19:30:07Z and 19:35:1xZ that this lane did not issue — read from the CloudScheduler.RunJob audit log, not inferred. They are included in the raw attempt log beside this artifact rather than left out. They did not change any job's configuration: all ten still carry this lane's secret hash (see configAfter) and no other writer touched the jobs. Recorded as an open thread, not as an explanation.

Cloud Logging's AttemptStarted timestamp runs a few seconds BEHIND the app's receipt time (e.g. wo-manager-sync AttemptStarted 19:05:17Z vs the app's authorized line at 19:05:16.467Z). The job's own lastAttemptTime agrees with the app, not with the log line. Do not treat the two clocks as the same when correlating.
